destination.name: Darwin
destination.tagline: Australia's northernmost capital, with crocodiles in the city centre, sunsets over the Timor Sea and the Top End on its doorstep.
destination.description: Darwin is the capital of the Northern Territory and Australia's only tropical capital, on Darwin Harbour and the Timor Sea. About 140,000 people live in this multicultural city, known for harbourside sunsets, markets and a crocodile attraction in the middle of town. It is the only Australian capital to have come under substantial attack in the war, with Japanese air raids from 1942, and Cyclone Tracy destroyed most of it in 1974. It is also the base for Litchfield, Kakadu and Nitmiluk, and for the wildlife parks and swimming holes south and east of the city.
whyVisit: Meet saltwater crocodiles at Crocosaurus Cove
Watch the sunset at Mindil Beach
See a B-52 bomber at the Aviation Museum

goodToKnow.title: Be crocwise
goodToKnow.detail: Any Top End water may hold crocodiles. Swim only where signed safe; box jellyfish are a danger from October to May.

goodToKnow.title: Wet and dry seasons
goodToKnow.detail: The Dry runs May to October; the Wet, November to April, brings storms and humidity. Book tours ahead in the Dry.

goodToKnow.title: Drink plenty of water
goodToKnow.detail: Drink at least two litres a day, wear a hat and sunscreen, and avoid walking in the hottest part of the day.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The Dry season, {months}, brings sunny days, lower humidity and the markets and festivals; the Wet is more humid, stormier and quieter.
